records.title: De Administrando Imperio
records.corpus_boundary: The fifty-three chapter diplomatic-administrative compilation conventionally titled De Administrando Imperio; later titles, excerpt collections, and related Constantinian compilations are excluded.

original_route.candidate: 1611 Greek-Latin edition in the University of Salamanca GREDOS repository; a later critical Greek edition remains preferable.

records.next_action: Inspect the GREDOS file and reuse terms; retain an explicit English gap unless a lawful older translation is located.

findings.proposition: University of Salamanca catalogs a 1611 Greek-Latin De Administrando Imperio edition.
Fordham's Byzantine source index identifies Constantine VII and the work as a distinct Byzantine source route.

unresolved_risks: The 1611 edition is not a modern critical text.
GREDOS file-level reuse terms require inspection.
The standard English translation remains restricted.

records.title: Chronographia
records.corpus_boundary: The Chronographia's imperial biographies only; Psellos's letters, philosophical works, and later continuations are excluded.

original_route.candidate: A Renauld-era Greek edition is bibliographically identifiable, but no stable reusable complete file was confirmed.

english_route.candidate: E. R. A. Sewter's complete 1953 English translation as displayed by Fordham.

records.next_action: Recover Fordham's file-specific publication basis and locate an institutional Greek edition before inspection.

findings.proposition: Fordham presents the entire Sewter English translation and identifies its 1953 lineage.
Princeton's Byzantine translation catalog identifies Psellos, Chronographia, and the modern English translation record.

unresolved_risks: Visible complete text does not establish portable reuse.
No Greek file is resolved.
No file has been inspected or admitted.

records.title: Kebra Nagast / Glory of the Kings
records.corpus_boundary: The received Ge'ez Kebra Nagast tradition; manuscript witnesses, modern Amharic renderings, and Budge's English translation remain separate bodies.

original_route.candidate: No exact institutional Ge'ez edition or manuscript-derived transcription was resolved.

english_route.candidate: E. A. Wallis Budge's 1932 English translation, surfaced through a Sacred Texts-derived mirror.

records.next_action: Locate an institutional Budge scan with an explicit rights statement and a named Ge'ez edition before downloading.

findings.proposition: The Sacred Texts-derived index identifies Budge, London, and 1932 for the English Kebra Nagast.
UNESCO Memory of the World provides the institutional discovery framework for manuscript heritage but does not by itself identify a reusable Ge'ez body.

unresolved_risks: The English route is a non-institutional mirror.
1932 rights require jurisdiction-specific review.
No Ge'ez body is located.

records.title: Ten Books of Histories / History of the Franks
records.corpus_boundary: Gregory's ten-book Histories; miracle collections and other works are excluded. Brehaut's 1916 English version is abridged and cannot represent the complete work.

original_route.candidate: A complete Latin critical body remains to be located in a stable institutional route.

english_route.candidate: Earnest Brehaut's abridged 1916 English translation, Library of Congress / Project Gutenberg lineage.

records.next_action: Inspect the LOC/Gutenberg file and encode abridgment boundaries; separately locate a Latin critical text.

findings.proposition: The Library of Congress catalogs Brehaut's 1916 History of the Franks and marks the collection item free to use and reuse.
Fordham explicitly labels its Brehaut text abridged.

unresolved_risks: The English body is incomplete by design.
No Latin counterpart is resolved.
A complete-work claim is unavailable.

records.title: Great Domesday and Little Domesday
records.corpus_boundary: Great and Little Domesday as distinct administrative witnesses; facsimiles, diplomatic transcriptions, normalized datasets, translations, and derived identifiers are separate layers.

original_route.candidate: National Archives facsimiles and Open Domesday/Hull scholarly data routes.

english_route.candidate: Modern Alecto/Penguin translation is restricted; normalized scholarly data may offer partial semantic access only.

records.next_action: Inspect the Hull dataset package, embedded license, schema, abbreviations, and derivation from Great versus Little Domesday.

findings.proposition: The National Archives distinguishes original records, paid facsimiles, Open Domesday, and modern printed translations.
University of Hull describes a downloadable scholarly Domesday dataset and its revised identifier layer.

unresolved_risks: Dataset license was not confirmed.
A dataset is not a facsimile or diplomatic transcription.
The complete modern English translation is restricted.

records.title: Summa Theologiae
records.corpus_boundary: The Summa Theologiae's Prima Pars, Prima Secundae, Secunda Secundae, Tertia Pars, and Supplement; commentaries and other Thomistic works are excluded.

original_route.candidate: Corpus Thomisticum Latin Summa route, pending file and reuse-term inspection.

english_route.candidate: Fathers of the English Dominican Province translation displayed by CCEL and New Advent.

records.next_action: Recover portable files and rights statements, then ledger every part and Supplement before completeness claims.

findings.proposition: Corpus Thomisticum exposes the Latin Summa as a dedicated scholarly text route.
CCEL identifies the English Dominican Fathers translation and provides a dedicated Summa work surface.

unresolved_risks: Web display does not prove bulk portability.
Latin and English edition alignment is unverified.
Multipart completeness requires a ledger.

records.title: Commedia / Divine Comedy
records.corpus_boundary: Inferno, Purgatorio, and Paradiso as one poem; commentary, illustrations, and later translations are separate bodies.

original_route.candidate: Project Gutenberg ebook 1000, complete Italian Divina Commedia.

english_route.candidate: Henry Francis Cary complete English translation, Project Gutenberg ebook 8800.

records.next_action: Inspect Gutenberg 1000 and 8800 byte-for-byte; identify the Italian editorial base and keep translation equivalence unclaimed.

findings.proposition: Project Gutenberg ebook 1000 supplies the complete Italian Divina Commedia route.
Project Gutenberg ebook 8800 identifies Henry Francis Cary and marks the English text public domain in the United States.

unresolved_risks: The Italian editorial lineage needs exact recovery.
No Italian/English equivalence claim is supported.
Gutenberg jurisdiction warnings must be preserved.

records.title: Mishneh Torah; Guide of the Perplexed
records.corpus_boundary: Mishneh Torah and Guide of the Perplexed are separate principal works; the Guide's Judeo-Arabic manuscripts, Hebrew translations, and English editions are distinct witnesses.

original_route.candidate: Library of Congress / National Library of Israel Judeo-Arabic Guide manuscript images, dated circa 1200.

english_route.candidate: M. Friedländer's 1904 revised English Guide, Internet Sacred Text Archive.

records.next_action: Inspect the LOC manifest and Friedländer body; separately research complete Mishneh Torah Hebrew and English routes.

findings.proposition: The Library of Congress identifies a circa-1200 Judeo-Arabic Guide manuscript, supplies a IIIF manifest, and states no known reuse restrictions for the collection item.
Sacred Texts identifies Friedländer's 1904 revised English translation and asserts United States public-domain status.

unresolved_risks: Manuscript images are not a clean transcription.
Mishneh Torah remains unresearched in this batch.
No cross-witness equivalence is established.

records.title: Kuzari / Kitab al-Khazari
records.corpus_boundary: The five-part Kuzari; the original Judeo-Arabic, Ibn Tibbon Hebrew translation, Hirschfeld Arabic edition, and English translation are distinct bodies.

original_route.candidate: Hartwig Hirschfeld's 1905 Arabic-and-English edition, Internet Archive identifier judahhalleviskit00judauoft.

english_route.candidate: Hirschfeld's complete 1905 English translation at Wikisource / Internet Archive.

records.next_action: Inspect the Internet Archive scan and OCR together; determine whether its Arabic layer is the edited Judeo-Arabic text and preserve the Hebrew gap.

findings.proposition: Open Library identifies the 1905 Hirschfeld edition as English and Arabic and links Internet Archive identifier judahhalleviskit00judauoft.
Wikisource presents all five parts of Hirschfeld's 1905 translation and marks the historical edition public domain.

unresolved_risks: OCR quality and scan completeness are uninspected.
The relation between edited Arabic and medieval Judeo-Arabic witnesses needs modeling.
No Hebrew body is resolved.

records.title: Muruj al-dhahab / Meadows of Gold
records.corpus_boundary: Muruj al-dhahab only; the nine-volume Barbier de Meynard/Pavet de Courteille Arabic-French edition, Sprenger's partial English translation, and later abridgments remain separate bodies.

original_route.candidate: Nine-volume 1861–1877 Arabic-French edition at Internet Archive, beginning with lesprairiesdor01masduoft.

english_route.candidate: Aloys Sprenger's 1841 English volume is partial; no complete English translation was located.

records.next_action: Build and inspect a nine-volume file ledger; verify item-level rights and reject one-volume English completeness claims.

findings.proposition: The historical Arabic-French Muruj edition is a nine-volume 1861–1877 sequence with stable Internet Archive identifiers.
The University of Halle catalogs the Barbier de Meynard/Pavet de Courteille edition and Arabic language metadata.

unresolved_risks: All nine volumes require reconciliation.
Item-level rights and OCR quality remain uninspected.
No complete English body is known.
